# About This Document

I developed this code to collect import and export data for various relevant critical minerals from the UN Comtrade API.

# Preparation and Set UP

## Installing packages and Inputting API Key

I have received two API keys through my UN Comtrade account. I now will install the r package and enter my API key.

```{r}
install.packages("comtradr")

library(comtradr)


set_primary_comtrade_key()
```

## Testing API Functionality

Now that the key is connected for this session, I will test if it is working.

```{r}

cobalt_data <- ct_get_data(
  reporter = "all_countries",
  partner = "World",
  commodity_code = "260500",
  flow_direction = "export",
  start_date = 2023,
  end_date = 2023
)

View(cobalt_data)
```

It worked for one year. I will try retrieving five years worth of data now. (Note: 260500 is the code for cobalt ores and concentrates)

```{r}

cobalt_5years <- ct_get_data(
  reporter = "all_countries",
  partner = "World",
  commodity_code = "260500",
  flow_direction = "export",
  start_date = 2020,
  end_date = 2024
)

View(cobalt_5years)
```

Great, this is working as well.

# Table of minerals and commodity codes

```{r}

library(comtradr)

library(readr)

products <- data.frame(
  mineral = c(
    "Cobalt", "Cobalt",
    "Lithium", "Lithium",
    "Rare Earths", "Rare Earths", "Rare Earths"
  ),
  product = c(
    "Cobalt ores",
    "Cobalt intermediates",
    "Lithium carbonate",
    "Lithium oxide and hydroxide",
    "Rare earth metals",
    "Cerium compounds",
    "Other rare earth compounds"
  ),
  hs_code = c(
    "260500", "810520",
    "283691", "282520",
    "280530", "284610", "284690"
  )
)

print(products)
```

# Reusable function

```{r}

dir.create("data/raw", recursive = TRUE,
           showWarnings = FALSE)

get_mineral_trade <- function(hs_code, mineral, product,
                              start_year, end_year) {

  # Divide the years into five-year blocks
  start_years <- seq(start_year, end_year, by = 5)

  results <- list()

  for (year in start_years) {

    final_year <- min(year + 4, end_year)

    # File where this API response will be stored
    filename <- paste0(
      "data/raw/", hs_code, "_",
      year, "_", final_year, ".rds"
    )

    if (file.exists(filename)) {

      # Reuse previously downloaded data
      data <- readRDS(filename)

    } else {

      message("Downloading: ", product,
              " | ", year, "-", final_year)

      data <- ct_get_data(
        reporter = "all_countries",
        partner = "World",
        commodity_classification = "HS",
        commodity_code = hs_code,
        flow_direction = c("Import", "Export"),
        start_date = year,
        end_date = final_year
      )

      # Save data so we don't download it again
      saveRDS(data, filename)
    }

    if (nrow(data) > 0) {
      data$mineral <- mineral
      data$product <- product

      results[[length(results) + 1]] <- data
    }
  }

  if (length(results) == 0) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  # Combine all five-year blocks
  bind_rows(results)
}
```

### Testing Function

```{r}

test_data <- get_mineral_trade(
  hs_code = "283691",
  mineral = "Lithium",
  product = "Lithium carbonate",
  start_year = 2022,
  end_year = 2024
)

View(test_data)
```

This worked. Now, I will test data quality/consistency

# Data Quality Testing

```{r}


# Number of observations
nrow(test_data)

# Observations by year and trade direction
table(test_data$period, test_data$flow_desc)

# Product description and classification
unique(test_data[
  c("cmd_code", "cmd_desc", "classification_code")
])
```

```{r}

# Count observations by year and HS classification
library(dplyr)

test_data |>
  count(period, classification_code) |>
  arrange(period, classification_code)
```

This shows that not all reports are using the same hs classification code. However, after looking into the historical hs codes for lithium carbonate, it seems that the six-digit number has remained the same throughout different versions of hs code classifications so it's not necessarily an issue for this specific mineral. however, it would be important to check that other minerals have also retained the same six-digit code throughout various versions of hs classification codes, and account for any changes in the six digit codes over the years.

```{r}


# Test all minerals in two historical periods

test_results <- list()

for (i in seq_len(nrow(products))) {

  for (start in c(1995, 2022)) {

    end <- if (start == 1995) 1999 else 2024

    result <- get_mineral_trade(
      hs_code = products$hs_code[i],
      mineral = products$mineral[i],
      product = products$product[i],
      start_year = start,
      end_year = end
    )

    if (!is.null(result)) {
      test_results[[length(test_results) + 1]] <- result
    }
  }
}

# Combine the results
mineral_test <- dplyr::bind_rows(test_results)
```

```{r}

library(dplyr)

classification_summary <- mineral_test |>
  group_by(mineral, product, cmd_code,
           classification_code, cmd_desc) |>
  summarise(
    observations = n(),
    first_year = min(as.integer(period)),
    last_year = max(as.integer(period)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(mineral, product, first_year)

View(classification_summary)


# Summarize product availability across our two periods

coverage_summary <- mineral_test |>
  group_by(mineral, product, cmd_code) |>
  summarise(
    total_observations = n(),
    records_1990s = sum(as.integer(period) <= 1999),
    records_2020s = sum(as.integer(period) >= 2022),
    classification_versions = n_distinct(classification_code),
    descriptions = n_distinct(cmd_desc),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

View(coverage_summary)
print(coverage_summary)


```

There are some issues with cobalt intermediaries to look into. The code 810520 was used in 2020s but not in 1990s. It seems that this is the reason: Before 2002: Code 810510 covered cobalt intermediates, unwrought cobalt, powders, and waste and scrap. From 2002: These were separated into 810520 for intermediates, unwrought cobalt and powders, and 810530 for waste and scrap

```{r}

cobalt_old <- ct_get_data(
  reporter = "all_countries",
  partner = "World",
  commodity_classification = "HS",
  commodity_code = "810510",
  flow_direction = c("Import", "Export"),
  start_date = 1995,
  end_date = 1999
)

# Examine historical descriptions
cobalt_old |>
  count(period, classification_code, cmd_desc)


cobalt_old |>
  distinct(classification_code, cmd_code, cmd_desc)

```

So here we see that with the older code 810510 cobalt information is available and the API is retrieving it. The issue is this cannot be combined with newer cobalt data as it uses a different description (discussed above).[**This is something to keep in mind during interpretation**]{.underline}.

```{r}
mineral_test_clean <- mineral_test |>

    !is.na(cmd_code),

    !is.na(flow_desc)

# Confirm that invalid records were removed
nrow(mineral_test_clean)
```

# Importing data

The code below imports data EXCEPT for the historical cobalt data

```{r}

# Create a list to store each product's data
all_results <- list()

# Loop through all seven mineral products
for (i in seq_len(nrow(products))) {

  message("Collecting: ", products$product[i])

  all_results[[i]] <- get_mineral_trade(
    hs_code = products$hs_code[i],
    mineral = products$mineral[i],
    product = products$product[i],
    start_year = 1995,
    end_year = 2024
  )
}

# Combine all results into one dataset
mineral_trade_raw <- dplyr::bind_rows(all_results)

# Remove records missing essential identifiers
mineral_trade <- mineral_trade_raw |>
  dplyr::filter(
    !is.na(cmd_code),
    !is.na(period),
    !is.na(flow_desc)
  )

# Save the combined dataset
readr::write_csv(
  mineral_trade,
  "data/mineral_trade_1995_2024.csv"
)
```
